- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp downward trend, reduce the forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the upward movement to prevent overshoot.  
- After a recent price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast to allow a slight lagged rebound.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often underestimates mean reversion — increase forecast mid-range to reflect gradual pullback.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply a downward bias correction of 1–2% per 5-day window.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals, model overfits to recent noise — smooth forecast with 3–5 day moving average.
